correctness.rationale: The graph is specified by 30 GP(10,3) edges and independently by incidence between 2-subsets and 3-subsets of five elements. The complement of each perfect matching in a cubic graph is a two-factor; a connected two-factor is Hamiltonian. Exhaustive least-unmatched-vertex recursion lists exactly 60 matchings, 24 of which have Hamiltonian complements. All 276 unordered Hamiltonian pairs were checked for a connected, two-regular symmetric difference: exactly 84 ten-edge trades, 60 eighteen-edge trades and 132 disconnected differences. A distinct direct Hamiltonian-path enumerator reproduces 24 states and the same trades. All 24 root BFS searches give shells (1,7,16), and all local neighborhoods are explicitly tested to be connected five-cycles and two isolates. Both packaged standalone programs were executed successfully with their asserted full checks, including the two edge-symmetry orbits. No infinite extrapolation is made.

General complexity results neither count these configurations nor establish their ten-move distances.

The Desargues perfect-matching hexagon/octagon theorem has 60 states and 180 combined edges with radius and diameter four under different move lengths.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Identical word “decagon” does not imply identical graph, as the Tutte–Coxeter base graph is not isomorphic to the Desargues graph. Perfect-matching 6/8-flip connectivity of the full 60-state space does not imply 10-flip connectedness of the constrained 24-state subspace. Bichromatic Kempe switching acts on full edge-colour partitions, not Hamiltonian-cycle edge sets. Thus the strongest concrete examined published results neither state nor imply the final 24-state geometry.

originality.rationale: Exact published-finding corpus similarity queries and primary literature were checked by implications, aliases and graph/move equivalences. The 60-state Desargues matching 6/8-flip classification, the 32-state Desargues Kempe graph and the 144-state Tutte–Coxeter Hamiltonian decagon graph do not cover or imply the 24-state Desargues Hamiltonian ten-trade adjacency geometry. General published perfect matching and Hamiltonian 2-edge switches use incompatible moves. Static 24-state cardinality is credited as prior work. The inspected strongest full records and metadata did not locate an exact previous statement. Historical priority remains uncertain for unindexed mathematical papers.
residual_risks: Some older works under alternating-cycle trades, 5-opt or Hamiltonian tour switching may not be indexed or accessible.

Literature absence is not a proof of mathematical novelty.

value.rationale: The sharp minimum trade size ten, uniform two-move reachability and explicit C5-plus-two-isolates local geometry give a structural description of Hamiltonian-tour flexibility on the natural symmetric cubic Desargues graph. The two distinct symmetry orbits of 84 trades separate different mechanisms of local mobility and permit a comparison with previously analyzed larger cubic Hamiltonian trade graphs. This is not a routine recount of known 24 Hamiltonian cycles or an unmotivated arbitrary parameter slice: it is a complete classification of naturally defined reconfiguration under constrained alternating-cycle exchanges.
